metadata.title: Add Raw HTML Download to Bronze Layer

story.iWant: to download and cache raw HTML as a bronze layer asset
story.soThat: content can be reprocessed without re-downloading from source URLs
story.tasks:
- Task 1: Create bronze_raw_html asset (AC: 1, 2, 4) - Create new file dagster_project/assets/bronze_raw_html.py - Define asset function bronze_raw_html(context: AssetExecutionContext, bronze_raw_links: list) -> list - Add asset decorator with io_manager_key, compute_kind, group_name, tags - Add dependency on bronze_raw_links via function parameter - Import httpx for HTTP downloads
- Task 2: Implement HTML download logic with caching (AC: 2, 3, 6) - For each URL compute full SHA256 hash - Check if artifacts/bronze/raw_html/{hash}.html exists (cache hit) - If cached: Skip download, log cache hit - If not cached: Download HTML using httpx.get() with timeout - Store raw HTML content, status code, headers, download timestamp - Use structlog for logging
- Task 3: Implement error handling (AC: 5) - Wrap httpx requests in try/except blocks - Catch HTTP errors (timeouts, 4xx, 5xx) - Store error metadata with url, error message, status_code, timestamp - Log errors using structlog - Continue processing remaining URLs
- Task 4: Verify BronzeIOManager handles HTML storage (AC: 3, 4, 6) - Review dagster_project/resources/io_managers.py implementation - Verify it handles raw HTML data structure - Verify storage in artifacts/bronze/raw_html/ subdirectory - Verify full SHA256 hash for filenames - Enhance if needed
- Task 5: Update asset exports (AC: 1) - Add bronze_raw_html to dagster_project/assets/__init__.py - Update __all__ to export new asset
- Task 6: Create integration tests (AC: 7) - Create tests/integration/test_bronze_html_download.py - Test HTML download and storage - Test cache hit behavior - Test full SHA256 hash filenames (64 chars) - Test metadata structure - Test error handling - Mark with @pytest.mark.integration
- Task 7: Verify content extraction compatibility (AC: 8) - Review dagster_project/ops/html_extractor.py - Verify can read from bronze cache structure - Document changes needed for Story 1.6
- Task 8: Run all tests and quality checks (AC: 7) - Run uv run pytest - Run make check - Verify no regressions

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: AC1: New asset bronze_raw_html created that depends on bronze_raw_links - Asset file exists with dependency declared AC2: Downloads raw HTML for each link using httpx - Integration test verifies HTTP download AC3: Stores raw HTML with metadata (url, download_timestamp, status_code, headers) - JSON structure verified in tests AC4: Uses BronzeIOManager for storage in artifacts/bronze/raw_html/ - Asset decorated with io_manager_key="bronze_io_manager" AC5: Handles HTTP errors gracefully (stores error metadata) - Test verifies error metadata storage for failed downloads AC6: Uses full SHA256 hash of URL for filename - Integration test verifies 64-char hash filenames AC7: Integration test verifies HTML download and storage - End-to-end test passes AC8: Existing content extraction can read from bronze cache - Verify html_extractor can load cached HTML (prep for Story 1.6)

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification: Medallion Architecture Migration
doc.snippet: bronze_raw_html asset downloads HTML via HTTP and caches to bronze layer. Raw HTML stored with metadata: url, status_code, headers, download_timestamp, error (if failed). html_extractor op reads from bronze cache instead of direct HTTP requests.

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification
doc.snippet: JSON metadata includes: url, status_code, headers, html_content (full raw HTML), download_timestamp (ISO 8601), created_at (ISO 8601), error (if HTTP error occurred)

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification
doc.snippet: bronze_raw_html checks if {hash}.html exists in bronze cache before downloading. If exists: Read from cache, skip download. If not exists: HTTP GET and save to cache. Simple file-existence check approach instead of partitioning.

doc.title: Epic Breakdown
doc.section: Story 1.5: Add Raw HTML Download to Bronze Layer
doc.snippet: New asset bronze_raw_html depends on bronze_raw_links, downloads raw HTML using httpx, stores with metadata in artifacts/bronze/raw_html/, handles HTTP errors gracefully, uses full SHA256 hash filenames, enables reprocessing from cache.

doc.title: Architecture Documentation
doc.snippet: Bronze layer stores raw, immutable data exactly as ingested. raw_html/ subdirectory caches downloaded HTML content. Enables reprocessing without re-downloading. No business logic applied in bronze layer.

doc.title: Story 1.2: Implement Bronze Layer IOManager
doc.snippet: BronzeIOManager handles storage of raw HTML content with metadata. Implementation includes _handle_output_html() and _load_input_html() methods with full SHA256 hashing and created_at timestamps.

doc.title: Story 1.4: Migrate Link Ingestion to Bronze Layer
doc.snippet: Asset naming: {layer}_{data_type} convention. IOManager integration via io_manager_key decorator. Assets return plain data; IOManager handles serialization. Full SHA256 hash (64 chars) for filenames. Use structlog for bronze layer logging.

artifact.reason: Bronze layer IOManager already implemented. Handles HTML storage via _handle_output_html() (lines 90-114) and _load_input_html() (lines 116-139). Expects dict with html_content field, generates full SHA256 hash, stores in raw_html_dir with created_at timestamp.

Upstream dependency for bronze_raw_html. Returns List[str] of unprocessed URLs. Demonstrates bronze layer asset pattern: io_manager_key, structlog logging, compute_kind, group_name, tags. Use as template for bronze_raw_html structure.
Helper function for SHA256 hash generation (truncated [:16] for legacy compatibility). For this story, compute FULL SHA256 hash directly (64 chars) for filename generation.
Current HTML extraction op that downloads HTML directly via httpx.get() (line 24). Story 1.6 will update this to read from bronze cache. Verify compatibility with bronze cache structure (AC8).
Asset exports module. Must add bronze_raw_html to imports and __all__ list for Dagster asset discovery (Task 5).

python.package: HTTP client for downloading HTML content with timeout support
Asset decorator, AssetExecutionContext, Field config schema
Structured logging for bronze layer operations
Path handling for file existence checks and directory operations
SHA256 hash generation for filename uniqueness

story-context.constraints: - Asset must follow bronze layer naming convention: bronze_raw_html (pattern: {layer}_{data_type}) - Asset decorator must include: io_manager_key="bronze_io_manager", compute_kind="python", group_name="bronze_layer", tags={"layer": "bronze", "source": "download"} - Asset must declare dependency via function parameter: bronze_raw_html(context: AssetExecutionContext, bronze_raw_links: list) - Asset returns plain data structure (list of dicts); BronzeIOManager handles serialization and file writing - Use full SHA256 hash (64 chars) for filenames, NOT truncated [:16] version - Use structlog for all logging (not context.log) to maintain bronze layer consistency - File-based caching strategy: Check if artifacts/bronze/raw_html/{hash}.html exists before downloading - Error handling must be resilient: HTTP failures stored as error metadata, don't fail entire batch - No direct file I/O in asset code - IOManager handles all persistence - HTTP downloads must include timeout parameter to prevent hanging - Store metadata in dict: url, html_content, status_code, headers, download_timestamp, error (if failed) - BronzeIOManager expects dict with "html_content" field for HTML type detection (see io_managers.py:22)

interface.name: BronzeIOManager._handle_output_html
interface.description: Expects dict with keys: url (str), html_content (str), download_info (dict, optional). Generates SHA256 hash from URL, adds created_at timestamp, stores in artifacts/bronze/raw_html/{hash}.json

interface.name: bronze_raw_links asset output
interface.description: Returns List[str] of unprocessed URLs. Use as input parameter for bronze_raw_html asset dependency

interface.name: httpx.get
interface.signature: httpx.get(url: str, timeout: int, follow_redirects: bool) -> Response
interface.description: HTTP client for downloading HTML. Use with timeout parameter (e.g., 30 seconds). Access response via response.text, response.status_code, response.headers

tests.standards: Integration tests use pytest with @pytest.mark.integration marker. Tests use tmp_path fixture for isolated test environments. Dagster testing utilities: build_asset_context() for asset execution, PropertyMock for config injection, OutputContext for IOManager testing. Bronze layer tests follow pattern from test_bronze_layer_migration.py: setup test environment with input files and directories, execute asset, verify IOManager storage, validate file structure and metadata. All tests must verify full SHA256 hash length (64 chars) for filenames.
tests.locations: tests/integration/ for multi-component end-to-end tests. Create new file: tests/integration/test_bronze_html_download.py for this story's integration tests.

ideas.test: Test HTML download and bronze storage - Create test URLs, execute bronze_raw_html asset, verify HTML content downloaded and stored via BronzeIOManager in artifacts/bronze/raw_html/
Test cache hit behavior - Run asset twice with same URLs, verify second run skips download (cache hit), check structlog output for cache hit messages
Test full SHA256 hash filenames - Verify all created files use 64-char hash (not truncated [:16]), check filename pattern matches {full_sha256}.json
Test metadata structure - Load saved JSON, verify contains url, html_content, status_code, headers, download_timestamp, created_at fields
Test HTTP error handling - Mock httpx.get() to raise HTTPError, verify asset continues processing remaining URLs, verify error metadata stored with error field populated
Test timeout handling - Mock httpx.get() with timeout exception, verify graceful error handling and error metadata storage
Test dependency on bronze_raw_links - Verify asset receives List[str] from bronze_raw_links upstream dependency
